quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results release, named customers: new core genomics customers signed include Nova Scotia Health Authority (HemOnc), DB Diagnósticos (Brazil, Rare Disorders) and IPO Lisboa (Hereditary Cancer); U.S. go-lives completed at Geisinger Health System (Pharmacogenomics), University of Illinois at Chicago (HemOnc) and NYU Langone Health (Solid Tumors); new MSK-ACCESS liquid biopsy customers include AZ Delta Roeselare (Belgium), Policlinico Riuniti Hospital at the University of Foggia (Italy) and Sultan Qaboos Cancer Center (Oman); new MSK-IMPACT solid tumor customers include Lifera Omics (Saudi Arabia), CHU Lyon Sud of Hospices Civils de Lyon (France) and Bioma Genetics (Brazil). SOPHiA signed a strategic collaboration with Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) to develop and launch a next-generation liquid biopsy application designed for pediatric cancers, and says recently signed BioPharma projects with AstraZeneca, Kartos and others began to generate revenue in Q2 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: liquid biopsy application MSK-ACCESS signed by 80 customers across 30+ countries (more than half still yet to complete implementation)

quarterly_data.signal: Partnerships (MD&A): in June 2026 SOPHiA signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) relating to the formation of a joint venture; the MOU envisions a precision medicine hub combining MSK's clinical data and expertise with SOPHiA's AI platform, which the company says could provide biopharma partners dedicated infrastructure for next-generation companion diagnostics, clinical algorithm development and evidence generation. Through previous license agreements for MSK assays (MSK-IMPACT, MSK-ACCESS) SOPHiA has brought MSK diagnostics to hospitals, labs and patients in 35 countries using SOPHiA DDM. In January 2026 it announced a strategic collaboration with The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, including co-developing an advanced next-generation sequencing oncology test; MD Anderson researchers will use SOPHiA's AI technologies to create bioinformatics pipelines for RNA-sequencing data.
quarterly_data.figure: MSK diagnostics deployed in 35 countries via SOPHiA DDM

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 interim statements and outlook: SOPHiA DDM Platform revenue $22,505 thousand vs $17,880 thousand (workflow equipment and services $805 thousand vs $443 thousand); United States revenue $4,341 thousand vs $2,660 thousand; gross margin 64.6% reported and 72.1% adjusted (67.0% / 74.4% a year earlier), lower as BioPharma and services grow. 2026 outlook adds an adjusted EBITDA loss of $29 million to $32 million, compared to $41.5 million in FY 2025. The company's minimum purchase agreement with a vendor for computational and hosting-related costs (approximately CHF 64.1 million ($79.3 million) from November 1, 2022 through October 31, 2029) had remaining commitments of CHF 40.6 million ($50.2 million) at June 30, 2026, versus CHF 44.4 million ($58.2 million) at December 31, 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: DDM Platform revenue $22,505 thousand; U.S. revenue $4,341 thousand; FY2026 adjusted EBITDA loss guidance $29 million-$32 million; remaining compute/hosting commitment CHF 40.6 million ($50.2 million)
